command.reason: Locate the loose hook frame, the stand opening, and the tool in calibrated world coordinates before selecting a grasp.
Grasp the dark junction of the loose hook frame from above and lift it clear of the table to verify acquisition before turning its long leg toward the stand.
The frame remained on the table and the fingers closed fully. Retry with the finger pads lower around the frame junction and allow the descent to settle before closing.
The frame lifted with the gripper. Raise it above the stand and turn the long insertion leg downward while maintaining the grasp.
Measure the suspended frame tip and stand opening to compute the horizontal alignment needed for insertion.
Translate the downward frame leg over the stand and lower its tip to just above the opening for a visual alignment check.
The insertion leg is directly above the stand opening. Lower it into the stand in two bounded stages while keeping its orientation fixed.
The frame reached a firm depth limit with its leg inside the stand. Release it at the measured pose and withdraw to check whether the stand supports it.
The open gripper still contacts the frame during withdrawal. Back away along the gripper's approach axis to clear the frame, then lift for an unobstructed inspection.
The released frame remains supported by the stand but has shifted. Measure the exposed hook and tool ends to plan hanging the tool in its actual settled configuration.
The frame is seated with its hook projecting toward positive world x. Grasp the tool's central handle from above and lift it so an end hole can be placed over the hook tip.
The tool did not lift. Measure its handle and hole rims in the closer wrist view to correct the grasp center and depth.
Center the fingers on the measured handle and settle lower before closing, then lift to verify that the tool is held.
The tool is visibly held. Measure the hole rim relative to the gripper and the upturned hook tip for accurate placement.
Turn the tool so its handle extends outward from the stand, then position its end hole above the upturned hook tip with clearance for lowering.
The wrist view shows the hook centered through the tool hole. Lower the horizontal hole over the upturned tip before rotating the handle downward.
Rotate the tool handle downward around the engaged hole while sliding the hole slightly inward along the horizontal hook.
The hook is visible through the tool hole. Complete the downward rotation and move the hole farther behind the upturned tip so the tool can hang vertically.
The tool is vertical and the hook passes through its upper hole. Release the handle, retreat outward from the tool, and move aside to verify that it remains hanging without gripper support.
The hook frame remains seated in the stand, and the released tool hangs vertically by its upper hole on the hook. The open gripper has withdrawn clear of the assembly.

scope: Offline measurements, not automatic causal attribution. Raw wrist loads include gravity and dynamics.
